column3: The Hebrew says “all Israel”; BSB says “Israel.”
The Hebrew calls Zabud the king’s “friend”; BSB uses “adviser.”
The Hebrew says “all the region of Dor”; BSB uses the place designation “Naphath-dor.”
The Hebrew repeats “belonged to him” for the two territories and uses singular “wall” and “bar”; BSB combines the territories and uses plural “walls” and “bars.”
The Hebrew says “one governor who was in the land,” without naming Judah; BSB adds “of Judah.”
The Hebrew says “the River” without naming it; BSB identifies it as the Euphrates.
The Hebrew uses “bread” for the daily provisions; BSB says “provisions.”
The Hebrew leaves the ruler unnamed, says “beyond the River,” and names “kings”; BSB supplies Solomon, specifies the west of the Euphrates, and uses “kingdoms.”
The Hebrew says “forty thousand” stalls and “twelve thousand horsemen”; BSB has 4,000 stalls and 12,000 horses.
The Hebrew repeats “King Solomon”; BSB uses “his” in the second occurrence.
The Hebrew uses the image “breadth of heart”; BSB renders this as “understanding beyond measure.”
The Hebrew says “sons of the East”; BSB uses “men of the East.”
